title: Biomes
examples: What factors determine what kind of plants grow in a biome?
Can you show me where different biomes are found around the world?
How does changing climate affect the boundaries of biomes?

explain.say: A biome is a large natural area with similar climate and plant life.
The climate includes things like average temperature and rainfall in a region.
Vegetation refers to the types of plants that naturally grow in that area.
The combination of climate and vegetation defines the biome's unique character.
The tropical rainforest biome has high rainfall and warm temperatures year round.
The desert biome has very low rainfall and can have extreme temperature changes.

faq.q: What is the main difference between a biome and an ecosystem?
faq.a: A biome is defined by its large-scale climate and dominant vegetation. An ecosystem is a more specific area including living and non-living things.
asks: Is a biome the same as an ecosystem?
How are biomes different from habitats?

faq.q: Do all biomes have the same types of animals?
faq.a: No, the animal life is also influenced by the climate and vegetation. For example, polar regions support different animals than tropical areas.
asks: What controls the wildlife in a biome?

faq.q: How do changes in temperature affect biome distribution?
faq.a: Rising temperatures can cause biomes to shift towards the poles or higher altitudes. This is called biome migration.
asks: What happens to biomes when it gets warmer?

faq.q: What causes the distribution of biomes across the globe?
faq.a: The main drivers are latitude, which affects temperature, and proximity to large bodies of water, which affects rainfall.
asks: What controls where biomes are found?

faq.q: Are there any biomes that exist only in one specific place?
faq.a: Some biomes are very localized, like certain types of alpine meadows. However, most major biomes have a wide distribution.
asks: Is any biome unique to one spot?

facts: Biomes are large areas characterized by similar climate and plant life.
Climate factors include average temperature and total annual rainfall.
The distribution of biomes is strongly influenced by latitude and altitude.
Tropical rainforests are characterized by high temperatures and high rainfall.

quiz.say: A region with very little rain and hot temperatures is likely a:
quiz.why: Deserts are defined by their low precipitation and often high temperatures.

wrong.1: Tundra is usually very cold, not necessarily hot.
wrong.2: Grasslands need more consistent rainfall than a desert.
wrong.3: Taiga is a forest biome, not defined by dryness.

quiz.say: If a region moves from a forest biome to a grassland biome, what has most likely changed?
quiz.why: A decrease in rainfall often causes forests to transition into grasslands.

wrong.1: Temperature change alone does not always cause this shift.
wrong.2: Changing latitude affects both temperature and rainfall.
wrong.3: Climate change is usually the primary driver of biome shifts.

quiz.say: Which pair of climate and vegetation best describes a temperate grassland?
quiz.why: Temperate grasslands receive moderate rainfall and are dominated by grasses.

wrong.0: This describes a rainforest, which is too wet.
wrong.1: This combination is more typical of a true desert.
wrong.2: This describes the tundra, which is much colder.
